outcome: The conjecture remains fully open. Since 26 January 2024 there has been a wave of uncoordinated preprints claiming constructive coverage of additional cases within the historically hardest residue classes (p ≡ 1 mod 4, and the six hard classes mod 840), computational verification extended to n ≤ 10^18, and one high-profile claimed full proof (Bradford, Feb 2026) that was publicly identified as flawed within days. None of this work has been digested or accepted by experts as settling any new case beyond what was already known before the frozen date, so I classify the overall movement as incremental, unverified 'progress' rather than 'partial' — no single one of these preprints has cleared the bar of expert digestion required by the record's own rules, and it is not this record's job to adjudicate between competing, mutually inconsistent, non-peer-reviewed claims about which classes are 'newly' covered.

ai.basis_quote: Tao referenced a ChatGPT Pro critique via a shared link when warning the community not to give credence to the claim without peer review; the AI was used to help evaluate/critique Bradford's claimed proof, not to produce any part of the mathematics in it.

disputes.summary: Kyle Bradford's February 2026 preprint (arXiv:2602.11774) claimed a full solution of the conjecture for all primes p via a covering-system argument over Type I/II solutions. A forum participant (StijnC) identified that 'taking the first primes modulo different moduli doesn't create a covering system' and noted the six hard residue classes mod 840 (per Mordell) were not excluded. Terence Tao publicly cautioned against crediting new solution claims absent peer review, citing a ChatGPT Pro critique of the argument. The arXiv listing shows only v1 (12 Feb 2026) with no withdrawal notice, so the paper has not been formally retracted, but the claim is treated as refuted/unverified by the community.

Several 2026 Zenodo postings under the pseudonymous author 'The Clankers' (e.g. records 19897796, 20019566, 21788700, 21806186, 21828422, 22678971), invoking invented terminology ('residual divisor shells', 'quotient surpluses', 'Star-Kneser theorem') and citing Reddit posts and a separate unrelated claim about Claude 'finding a counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture,' appear to be AI-generated crank content rather than genuine mathematics. They are excluded from this record's status/event determination but are noted here since they specifically claim heavy AI involvement in their own (non-credible) production.

summary: The classical Erdős–Straus conjecture (4/n = 1/x+1/y+1/z for all n≥2) remains open as of September 2026. No result in the window has been digested by experts as settling the conjecture or a clearly-new, verified case of it. What did happen: (1) computational verification was extended from n≤10^17 to n≤10^18 (Mihnea & Bogdan, arXiv:2509.00128, Aug 2025) — an existence-search extension that per §3.1 does not move an existence/infinitude-style bullet on its own, though here it is at least evidence-gathering on a question that already has a known-affirmative answer for all checked n; (2) a cluster of preprints (Dyachenko arXiv:2511.07465, Nov 2025; Farah, SSRN, Aug 2025 claiming 804/840 residue classes mod 840 explicitly plus a probabilistic bound on the rest; Ghermoul arXiv:2508.07383; Mballa arXiv:2602.20036; Xu arXiv:2605.23601; Bello-Hernández et al. arXiv:2606.10922) each claim constructive coverage of some sub-cases of the historically hardest class p≡1(mod4) or the six hard classes mod 840, none of them peer-reviewed, none cross-cited or reconciled with each other, and none discussed by Tao or on his blog (whose only Erdős-Straus posts remain from 2011); (3) a February 2026 preprint by Kyle Bradford (arXiv:2602.11774) claimed a full proof for all primes p via a covering-system argument, and was identified within days as flawed by a forum participant (the covering-system claim doesn't exclude the six hard classes mod 840), with Terence Tao publicly urging caution and referencing a ChatGPT Pro critique of the argument — this is the single clearest 'event' in the window and I have classified the record as status=progress/incident-flavored around it, since a claimed resolution was made and refuted, even though the arXiv listing shows no formal withdrawal. AI was used here only to critique/evaluate a human-produced (and flawed) claim, which the rules explicitly exclude from any ai_role other than none. I also found and deliberately excluded two false leads that share the 'Erdős' name: the OpenAI/DeepMind 2026 breakthroughs widely reported as solving '80-year-old Erdős problems' concern the unrelated unit-distance conjecture and other numbered problems on erdosproblems.com, not Erdős–Straus; and a genuine 2025/2026 Tao–Teräväinen result explicitly described as 'establishing a conjecture of Erdős and Straus' (arXiv:2512.01739) is about a totally different statement (ω(n+k) ≤ Ω(n+k) ≪ k for consecutive integers), sharing the same two mathematicians' names by coincidence, not a case or variant of the unit-fraction conjecture. I also found a cluster of pseudonymous 'The Clankers' Zenodo postings that read as AI-generated crank content with invented terminology and self-referential claims about Claude/AI producing 'counterexamples' to an unrelated conjecture; these are not credible mathematics and are excluded from the status determination, noted only in disputes.
competing_reading: One could argue for status=open with no_change_found=true, on the grounds that none of the incremental preprints meets any bar of expert verification and the one dramatic event (Bradford's claim) was refuted rather than being real progress — under a strict reading, 'progress' requires a bound that actually moved, and no expert has confirmed that the 804/840 or p≡1(mod4) claims genuinely extend prior published coverage (the field already had explicit families for large swathes of residues before 2024, e.g. via Mordell, Elsholtz, and others, and it is unclear from a non-expert read of these preprints whether they are genuinely novel or re-derive known results). I lean toward 'progress' primarily because of the Bradford incident, which is a concrete, dated, publicly-litigated event fitting the 'instructive incident' category in §6.1, but a stricter reading would call this open/no_change_found given the total absence of expert digestion of any of the claimed advances.
what_would_settle_it: Expert commentary (e.g. from Tao, Elsholtz, or a survey/journal referee) explicitly stating whether any of the 2024-2026 preprints (Dyachenko, Farah, Mballa, Xu, Bello-Hernández, Ghermoul) establish genuinely new coverage of residue classes beyond pre-2024 published results, and confirmation of whether Bradford's arXiv:2602.11774 was ever formally withdrawn or corrected.

corrections.by: judging pass (JUDGE.md), opus; not the researching agent and not a human reviewer
corrections.why: F6/F4: The status rested on Bradford's claim, which the record's disputes show was knocked down by a specific error: the covering system does not cover, and the six hard classes mod 840 are left out. A knocked-down claim is not progress. Verification to 10^18 is instances. The residue-class preprints move no bound, and the record itself doubts they go beyond pre-2024 coverage (Farah's 804/840 is below Mordell's classical 834/840). Nothing survives, so the status is open, as the record's competing_reading argued.

events.what: Bradford claims a full proof for all primes via a covering-system argument over Type I/II solutions
events.credibility_reason: Specific identified error in the key step, recorded in the record's disputes: 'taking the first primes modulo different moduli doesn't create a covering system', and the six hard residue classes mod 840 are not excluded. No answer from the author is recorded.

events.what: Cluster of preprints (Dyachenko, Farah, Ghermoul, Mballa, Xu, Bello-Hernández et al.) giving explicit families covering sub-classes of p ≡ 1 mod 4 or of the hard classes mod 840
events.credibility_reason: The record says it is unclear whether any of them go beyond pre-2024 coverage (Mordell, Elsholtz and others). Farah's 804/840 classes is fewer than the classical Mordell coverage of all but 6 of 840. Density-one explicit solutions were already known. Adding more covered congruence sub-classes does not settle any restriction of the bullet the literature did not already have. The preprints are mutually unreconciled and uncited.

events.credibility_reason: Pseudonymous, invented terminology, cites Reddit posts, no uptake on a landmark problem.

judgement.doubts: The Bradford claim fields (event, credited_humans) are left as the record's most salient event, but they set nothing. If an expert later confirms that one of the residue-class preprints covers a restriction that was genuinely new, it would be a case (partial). Nothing in the record shows that.
